name: NEON (South China Sea Neutrino Observatory)
summary: A proposed South China Sea optical telescope explores a large high-energy neutrino observatory complementary to existing global detectors.
detection_principle: Underwater strings of multi-photomultiplier optical modules would record Cherenkov light from neutrino-induced particles; the design is evaluated using detector simulations.

sites.name: China; candidate deep-sea site in the South China Sea
sites.location: China; candidate deep-sea site in the South China Sea

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The founding paper explicitly presents a proposed telescope; the 2026 PDG review retains it among future concepts.

timeline.event: Initial telescope concept and sensitivity study released.
Included in the PDG inventory of future neutrino-telescope concepts.

collaboration.name: NEON (South China Sea Neutrino Observatory) Collaboration

key_parameters.value: Multi-PMT optical modules in simulated string-array configurations

results.summary: Published sensitivity calculations describe a possible future telescope; no deployed full NEON neutrino observatory is established by these sources.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
